plants.name: Syringa vulgaris
plants.description: A deciduous shrub producing dense, conical clusters of intensely fragrant, small four-lobed flowers. It is a staple of cottage gardens and old homesteads and attracts butterflies and bees.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late spring (late April to early June in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to the Balkan Peninsula; widely cultivated across temperate North America, Europe, and northern Asia
plants.funFact: Lilac was the first plant used as a symbol of the Garden Club of America in some regions, and its scent is so beloved that perfumers recreate it synthetically, since the flowers yield little natural essential oil.

plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: A long-lived herbaceous perennial with large, lush, often double and fragrant blooms above glossy, deeply divided foliage. Peonies are prized as cut flowers and garden showpieces.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (May to June in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to Siberia, Mongolia, and northern China; cultivated worldwide in temperate gardens
plants.funFact: Peonies have been cultivated in China for over 1,500 years and some plants can live and bloom for more than 100 years. Ants on the buds are harmless and feed on the sugary nectar.

plants.name: Hyacinthoides non-scripta
plants.description: A bulbous woodland perennial that carpets forest floors with nodding, bell-shaped, sweetly scented violet-blue flowers all arching to one side of the stem.
plants.location: Native to the Atlantic coast of Western Europe, especially ancient woodlands of the United Kingdom
plants.funFact: About half of the world's bluebells grow in the UK, and they are legally protected there; it is illegal to dig up wild bulbs for sale. Bluebell woods often take 5-7 years to establish from seed.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A spectacular tree with fern-like leaves that erupts in clouds of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. In the Southern Hemisphere's late autumn, some trees can still be seen flowering in warm northern parts, while the Northern Hemisphere's subtropical populations begin blooming in May.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Northern Hemisphere subtropics (May to June); October to November in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to South America (Argentina, Bolivia); planted widely in Mexico, Southern California, Florida, the Mediterranean, and northern Africa
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, tens of thousands of jacarandas line the streets, earning it the nickname 'Jacaranda City', and in parts of Australia a falling bloom on your head is said to bring good luck.
